result: User reported that Oh Great played successfully through Pi 4B HDMI. A key stopped it after a delay of about a minute.
related_check: The user also reported hearing a note using the Psalmody z, h, x sequence on the same setup.
interpretation: The pinned song checks CharScan between complete playthroughs, so a key can wait until the current sequence finishes. The report confirms audible app playback and eventual stop, not precise timing or fidelity.
image_provenance: The running microSD image and kernel hash were not independently inspected during this report; do not attribute it to the current QEMU source bundle or a specific commit.

qemu_followup.target: QEMU HVF with VirtIO sound and WAV backend
qemu_followup.result: The same ExeFile2 command played until a late lyric, accepted a normal key, returned to the prompt after the remaining notes and executed 40+2 in the graphical terminal task. zstatus reported failed=0. The WAV contained 48.36 seconds of 44.1 kHz stereo PCM, 4261826 nonzero samples and a peak of 7000; frequency-window analysis found multiple pitches. This is evidence of sustained changing tones, not an exact audio-fidelity comparison.

limits: One Pi, one HDMI output and these two app-audio paths. Full music fidelity, other songs, headphone output for this song, live UTM playback and other Pi hardware remain unverified.
